paragraphs.text: Languages

Your race determines your starting languages. Your Background may grant additional languages. Standard languages like Common, Dwarvish, and Elvish facilitate most interactions, while Exotic languages like Abyssal, Celestial, or Draconic grant access to ancient texts, other-worldly beings, or specific cultural groups. Consider languages that complement your background and intended role. Here are the list of languages known and spoken in the game. There are several more that must be discovered (which are in the Dungeon Manual)Standard Languages by Race
Common – Widespread trade tongue across Aethel.
Elvish – Spoken by all elven variants (High, Wood, Twilight, Umbrin).
Dwarvish – Used by all dwarven types (Mountain, Forge, Deep).
Draconic – Language of the Drakari.
Gnomish – Used by all gnome subtypes.
Orcish – Tribal language spoken by all orc clans.
Goblin – Spoken by goblins and their underground kin.
Trollish – Rare, growling dialect unique to troll culture.
Aquan – Language of the amphibians and water-based creatures.
Mycelic (or Sporetongue) – Whispered pheromone-based language of the Mycelians.
Giant – Shared among ogres and other large ancient races.
Sylvan – Spoken by Feykin and creatures associated with the Verdant Reflection tradition.
Murkish – The spoken language of the denizens of The Murk used by Umbrin, Deep Dwarves, etc.
Imperial (Human script dialects) – Subset variants: Westreach, Eastern Sigil, and Northern Vale (can be combined under “Common” for mechanics, but distinct culturally).
Intelligent NPC or Special Languages
Celestial – Language of the First Choir and Ascended mortals.
Infernal – Tongue of devils, hell-bound mortals, and infernal contracts.
Abyssal – Chaotic language of demons and abyssal entities.
Primordial – Root language of the elements (spoken by storm elementals, druids of the Circle of the Storm).
Runic – Archaic script-based language used in dwarven high-forging and ancient enchantments.
The Voice – Musical-resonance dialect only understood by beings attuned to Calan’thir’s vibration (e.g. The First Voice, the Speaker, Archons).
Resonant Cant – Esoteric frequency-based tongue encoded in the architecture of the dungeon itself; decipherable by Mirrorsages, Tinkers, or beings with exposure to the Source.

spellComparisonRecords.name: Omen Whisper

operational.targets: One creature, object or location you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect; alternatively, one specific course of action you are considering beginning within the next minute in the current situation.
operational.resolution: No roll. The Director gives one brief, truthful, cryptic but usable phrase or sentence about the most immediately relevant circumstance, danger, opportunity or likely consequence connected to the chosen subject or proposed action.
operational.effect: Only you perceive and understand the whisper. It supplies a supernatural clue from current circumstances, including relevant hidden circumstances when their disclosure is permitted; it is not merely a cosmetic noise. Its wording may be symbolic but must convey a usable clue rather than deliberately contradict the relevant facts. No deity, spirit, speaker or binding promise is established. Recasting a materially equivalent inquiry about the same subject or proposed action while the materially relevant circumstances remain unchanged gives the same omen or a restatement, without cumulative extra detail. This equivalence applies across casters: rephrasing the inquiry, passing it to another caster, or subdividing it solely to extract additional detail about the same issue does not create new information. A genuinely different material question about that subject, or a material change in circumstances, may produce a different omen.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in targets, range, duration or information.
operational.limitations: It does not guarantee future decisions, dice or events not yet caused, compel anyone to enact a predicted outcome, reveal a whole stat block/inventory/plot or automatically succeed at a task. New voluntary actions or genuinely new causes may make a previously truthful omen obsolete. Rephrasing the same inquiry, switching casters or serially subdividing it does not create extra information from an unchanged omen; use the same materially equivalent subject/circumstance boundary. No additional daily use cap is added. If all relevant information is specifically protected, the Director gives only an uninformative opaque omen without naming the protection; permitted information about other subjects remains available. Actual class access and repertoire, audible V/free-hand S components, casting sequence, Refrain/Dissonance, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base RP is 0 but repeated cantrips still follow their actual strain rules. No automatic upcast or unstated scaling. Source-specific protections apply only to their actual scope. Protection from Scrying prevents new Divination/Scrying information about its protected subject, including beneficial inspection, but grants no blanket immunity to damage, buffs or other noninformational mechanics merely because of their school; it does not erase already-known facts or ordinary records.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30feet/V,S/instantaneous and a cryptic supernatural tip. NEW: bounded subject/action input, one truthful usable private clue, current-circumstances scope and no incremental detail for materially repeated inquiry. No universal future-certainty or spirit-contact ability.

spellComparisonRecords.name: Speak with Dead

operational.targets: One perceived corpse or substantial apparent creature remains within 60 feet and line of effect; eligibility of its deceased identity and retained memories resolves after casting costs commit.
operational.duration: Up to 1 minute or until five question exchanges are spent; no concentration. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; outside initiative, expires 60 elapsed seconds after application. Preserve the original virtual marker or absolute deadline through initiative changes, absence, death and planar travel. An already-passed start never counts.
operational.resolution: No save or willing-soul gate. After costs commit, determine whether these are sufficient actual remains of one currently dead creature identity to support an associated retained memory echo. Bones or equivalent substantial creature remains can qualify without an intact mouth, tongue or biological flesh. An active Undead/Construct, an ordinary broken device that was never a creature, identityless ash, a stray blood trace or old remains of a currently living identity do not qualify. If no readable qualifying echo exists, obtain no answers without learning which eligibility/protection fact failed.
operational.effect: Invoke a retained memory echo associated with the addressed remains and deceased identity, not a soul, creature or resurrection. For this application you may spend up to five question exchanges. Each attempted materially unified inquiry and its answer uses one Action in initiative, or approximately six elapsed seconds outside initiative, and one question allowance; the original casting Action includes no free question. Distinct independent subquestions require their own exchanges, Actions and allowances even when spoken as one sentence. You must audibly address the remains from within 60 feet and line of effect; ordinary sound-blocking conditions apply. Each committed exchange spends its allowance even if the question is not understood or its answer is unknown/protected. The echo answers audibly from the remains, truthfully according to the deceased’s actual associated memories and beliefs before death. It uses a language the deceased knew and would reasonably use, with no automatic translation. If no mutually usable language or remembered answer supports a response, it may provide no intelligible answer, I do not know, I do not remember, or the appropriate equivalent. It cannot deliberately lie or withhold a known readable answer from hostility, but mistaken beliefs remain mistaken.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, duration, targets, uses or information.
operational.limitations: Actual memories associated with the remains govern: this grants no post-death knowledge or automatic later-life memory update to an older fragment after resurrection and another death. Multiple fragments remain one deceased identity, not new people or duplicated souls. A fresh legal paid cast can ask another five; no daily immunity or exclusive global interview slot is added. Each application retains its own quota and deadline; asking an echo does not simultaneously question all other applications. The echo ends if the identity becomes living, the selected physical anchor no longer contains qualifying remains, the five exchanges are spent, or the spell expires/is actually ended. A temporary gap in speaking/range/sound/line of effect pauses no duration. Existing answers and ordinary remembered information persist after ending. Soul Bind or a resurrection-only blocker does not automatically block this memory echo; actual corpse, communication, memory or information protections keep their written scope. The spell generates Divination through Cleric, Mirrorsage, Ranger, Shaman, Wizard or Paladin, and Necromancy through Crimson Agent, Druid or Thief, exactly as the selected casting class’s access row states. A Divination-only ward cannot block a Necromancy cast merely because this shared identity has another school placement. Protection may also filter new information about a separately protected subject within its actual scope. No compelled living creature, identity creation, body animation, healing, resource refresh, skill/proficiency download, objective-history verification or usable recording token results. Actual class access, repertoire, V/S/F components, costs, Dissonance/Refrain, beginning hooks, concentration transitions and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Commit costs before the counter window; failed, blocked and countered effects do not refund costs or restore prior concentration. Use the actual casting class's school and rank. Specific information protections apply to their actual subjects and generating-source scope. Hidden unprotected facts are readable; undefined facts are not invented. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both rank-three Divination/Necromancy source placements and five questions/answers; Core M/F uses shared F. engine: Blood Gauge (BG) starts and ends each encounter at 0, capacity 3; Spill Control raises capacity 6 while known. Dexterity governs weapon attacks; Intelligence governs hemomancy save DC and M. S scales from Crimson Agent class level. Your Bleed is a physical ongoing effect on a living, non-bloodless creature: 1d4 damage at the start of each of its next 3 turns, then ends. It is not a new attack and generates no BG or procs. Refresh duration instead of stacking; Blood Echo expressly allows two independent instances, maximum. An Action by the victim or an adjacent creature using a healer's kit ends all your Bleeds on that victim. Apply physical resistance/immunity normally. Track remaining ticks and creator per instance. Allied healing versions from Bloodweaver cost RP and never count as hostile Bleeds for detonation, spreading or generation.

One Blood Mark at a time on a living target with your Bleed, except Phantom Strike, which explicitly may apply the mark without Bleed. It does not add a free Bleed. Marks last 5 of your regular turns, expire on encounter end or if the target dies, and never create damage by themselves. Rupture requires the target still within 60 ft and line of effect; it spends the mark. A mark does not defeat cover, planar boundaries or bloodlessness. Bloodtrail has its own tracking limits.

A form giving temporary HP draws that many from Buffer Reserve, up to remaining amount, with normal nonstacking; never real healing. A form special described once/transformation also spends 1 Form Surge and cannot be refreshed by resuming the form. Form Surge refills only long rest. Forms cannot grant free casts, RP or shift uses. Auras affect at most 3 enemies and once per enemy per round; retaliation once/round total; ongoing riders refresh, never stack. Entering a legal Shapeshift clears the Refrain counter and remembered repeated-spell name, as the protected source contract requires. It does not reduce accumulated Dissonance. Natural attacks do not clear Refrain.

Circle of the Land chooses one terrain at 2. Always-prepared spell pairs at 3/5/7/9 are exactly the source table lines 2662–2669, reproduced in source appendix; their source names resolve to existing approved spell entries before use. They do not bypass rank gates. For this pilot Circle spells are permitted exceptions to ordinary list membership, not newly authored variants. Moon Circle Forms CR table is historical external-stat language: use only these bounded forms, not arbitrary CR beasts. Early Moon benefit is +S damage on first form hit each turn. No imported monster multiattack, spellcasting or legendary actions.

Circle summary: Land preserves lore and recovery; Moon improves shifting; Storm controls lightning and wind; Thorns works poison and roots; Winterfang works cold; Rotshaper uses bounded swarms; Ashen Grove works fire and regrowth. Land/Thorns duplicate Blight Elk and Tanglemaw names are kept as separate source identities. Source auto-failed hostile saves in Master of Decay/Ash become once/turn-2 on one save, not unavoidable control. engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Mage class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Mage levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier) unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Mage spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Mage spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

Spellcasting and Resonance Pool are automatic class features, never selection taxes. Use the Mage maximum Resonance Point pool and ordinary spell-rank costs from authoritative Core Systems Known Descent V 2. All Mage card RP costs and ordinary spell RP costs come from that same pool. There are no spell slots. A long rest restores RP according to Core V 2; other existing recovery rules remain separate unless this pilot explicitly overrides them.

Named Mage cards tagged mage-spell, and the three Focus finishers are spells for Focus, Nuke Chain, Refrain, concentration, Counterspell and other spell-referencing mechanics. Their printed RP cost replaces an ordinary rank cost; do not charge both. Generic Overcast is disabled for these class-card spells during this pilot unless a card expressly enables it. They receive no extra class-level Burn or Dissonance simply for being card spells; ordinary Core V 2 spell-risk rules still apply where applicable.

Elemental Focus is gained automatically at Mage level 2. Choose Fire, Cold or Lightning and automatically gain the corresponding Focus card. Your selected Focus determines the element used by Elemental Bolt, Elemental Surge, your Focus finisher and other effects that refer to your chosen element. Unless Elemental Pivot or another explicit effect changes it, the choice is permanent in this draft.

NUKE CHAIN. Track your last three consecutive Focus-eligible spell casts. A Focus-eligible cast is a Mage or ordinary spell that deals your currently chosen Fire, Cold or Lightning damage type and is identified by a distinct spell or card name. A spell of another element or a non-elemental spell clears the chain. The last three eligible casts must have three different names. Repeating one chosen-element spell remains a legal cast but shifts the three-cast window and follows ordinary Refrain rules; repetition does not receive special protection from Dissonance.

When the third different named chosen-element spell in the current three-cast window resolves, complete the Nuke Chain, reduce Dissonance by 2 to a minimum of 0, and prime your selected Focus finisher until the end of your next regular Mage turn. Chain completion occurs whether targets hit or save, provided all three spells were legally cast and resolved. A finisher is not itself a chain-building spell. Using the finisher or allowing it to expire clears the chain and the primed state.

FOCUS FINISHERS. A primed Focus finisher is a Bonus Action Mage spell costing 2 RP and is usable once per completed Nuke Chain. Each finisher also has a 3-round recharge. A completed chain can prime a finisher whose recharge is still positive, but the primed use expires normally if the recharge does not become ready in time. Finisher recharge is subject to the universal positive-counter reset limit of once per ability per round.

RESONANCE SURGE. Once per short rest, when you begin casting a damaging Mage spell, you may spend 2 additional RP after validating the spell's normal cost. Add S d8 damage of one damage type already dealt by that spell to one of its damage rolls. Resonance Surge does not count as Overcast, does not independently alter Dissonance or Burn, does not create another spell cast, and does not advance the Nuke Chain separately.

Only one concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect ends the first. Damage prompts the current Core Systems concentration save; for this pilot any required half-damage rounding is down. Round recharge counters tick once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if incapacitated, and every uninterrupted 6 seconds outside initiative. Only positive counters may be shortened or reset and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions. Mage summons and companions do not receive independent damaging turns: all Mage-controlled conjured companions share one Companion Command per Mage regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one companion to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded companions may move to remain near you and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose control.

ELEMENTAL FAMILIAR. Conjure Elemental Familiar creates one familiar matching your current Focus; you may have only one elemental familiar. AC = 12 + PB; HP = 5 + Mage level + M; Speed 30 feet; Lightning familiar additionally has Fly 30 feet, Fire has resistance to fire, Cold has resistance to cold. It uses your saves and PB where required. Elemental Dart: ranged spell attack using your Mage spell attack, range 30 feet, hit S d4 damage of its element. It cannot generate RP, Dissonance, Focus casts, corpses, XP, loot or kill-trigger resources.

LICH COMPANION SYSTEM. A successful Lich transformation unlocks three unique bound elite companions: Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound. You can maintain at most one of each, maximum three total. They return at full HP after a completed long rest unless a campaign consequence expressly prevents it. A destroyed elite leaves no usable corpse and cannot generate XP, loot, RP, Nuke Chain credit, Soul Reservoir or kill-based resources. Soulbound Ritual can return one before a long rest.

BONEFLAYER. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 12 + 2 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Bone Shards: range 60 feet, your Mage spell attack, hit 2d6 + S necrotic. Fear Pulse: instead of Bone Shards, enemies of your choice within 10 feet make Wisdom saves against your Mage DC; failure causes Frightened until the end of their next turn; recharge 3 rounds. Grave Miasma: instead of Bone Shards, one 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet persists until the start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3 rounds.

DREADBLADE. Medium undead; AC 16; HP = 16 + 3 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Disrupting Blade: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. If the target is concentrating it immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20, the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 to attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

WRAITHBOUND. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 10 + 2 × Mage level; Fly 40 feet and can hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn, it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. On a natural 20, the target makes a Constitution save against your Mage DC; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

LICH TRANSFORMATION READINESS. At Mage level 10 a character may select Lich only after obtaining either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants, binding at least two named mini-bosses as guardians, securing a planar nexus and surviving the Director's divine-echo encounter. A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check. If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.

Before the irreversible Lich roll, the Director must explicitly tell the player the historical failure stakes: permanent loss of spellcasting, transformation into a cursed melee undead NPC, hostile faction consequences, cursed-gear restriction and no further XP as that retired PC. The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Mage 1 automatically gains Spellcasting, Resonance Pool and Resonance Surge, then chooses 4 eligible selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Mage 2 automatically chooses and gains one Elemental Focus card, then chooses 2 additional Base cards. Mage 3 enters Arcanist and chooses 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4 through 9 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch card; level 9 is an ordinary choice because the historical source has no Arch capstone.

At Mage 10 choose Archmage, Elementalist or, if its ritual succeeds, Lich; choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. Mage 20 grants one additional Hero-path choice plus the NEW playtest level-20 class capstone in extra Cards. No historical Hero Finale is implied. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition gates use Mage class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus remains the normal total-character proficiency bonus. Non-Mage levels do not unlock Elemental Focus, Arcanist, Hero cards, Nuke Chain upgrades, Lich ritual access or the level-20 Mage capstone.

Class-spell ranks are printed in the normalized card data: use the legal maximum Mage rank at that card's minimum class level, capped 9; the three Focus finishers are rank 1. Rank determines Dissonance, Counterspell and rank-limited interactions, not a second RP cost. A shared spell uses the ally's normal Action and caster-side Dissonance at the moment it is cast; it never builds the Mage's Nuke Chain remotely. Spellcasting through Fracture as Lich uses the shared direct-trauma rule.

engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Dexterity is the Monk class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Monk levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Dexterity modifier). Monk technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier. Monk technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier.

Ki Chain is a Monk-only resource from 0 to 5. Begin each real encounter at 0 Ki and clear Ki when the encounter ends or after 1 minute without a real encounter. Ki cannot be generated by sparring with willing creatures, attacking objects, repeatedly dodging harmless attacks, healing between encounters or other staged actions. Ki is separate from Resonance Points and Dissonance.

Normal Ki generation is capped at 2 Ki during your own regular turn and 1 Ki total from reactions or defensive events between the end of one regular turn and the start of your next. Explicit spending has no per-turn cap other than available Ki. A feature cannot raise Ki above 5. Incapacitation or Stunned resets Ki to 0; ordinary damage does not.

All Monks automatically know Tiger, Tortoise and Crane Stances at level 1. Only one core stance can be active at a time. While unarmored and not using a shield, you may switch to one known core stance on your own turn without an Action, at most once per round. The stance remains until changed, incapacitated or the encounter ends. The optional Stance Shift feature improves when that same once-per-round switch may occur; it does not create a second switch.

Unarmored Flow is automatic class identity rather than a selectable card. Wearing armor or using a shield suppresses the mechanical benefits printed on Tiger, Tortoise and Crane Stances, Unarmored Speed, Perfect Balance and Tortoise Discipline features unless a card explicitly says otherwise. Ki Chain itself and Monk techniques remain usable unless their card requires being unarmored.

Tiger, Tortoise and Crane Ki generation obey the global Ki-gain ceilings. Tiger can generate Ki from critical unarmed strikes. Tortoise can generate Ki from specified defensive successes. Crane provides mobility and support but does not create free out-of-combat healing. A single event can satisfy more than one generator, but total gain still cannot exceed the appropriate own-turn or off-turn ceiling.

MINOR WEAVE INTERFACE. Cards tagged weave are magical Monk techniques. If a tagged technique would add at least 1 Dissonance under the broader Weave rules, after validating all ordinary costs but before resolution you may spend 1 additional Ki to prevent that 1 Dissonance. This prevention Ki is separate from the card's printed Ki and RP costs. It cannot prevent more than 1 Dissonance from one technique and cannot reduce Dissonance already present.

All printed RP costs use the character's existing Resonance Point pool where applicable; Monk cards create no second RP pool. Ki never converts to RP unless a card explicitly says so. Generic spell-slot mechanics do not apply. Monk techniques are not ordinary spells unless their card expressly says otherwise.

STUN GUARD. A creature can be Stunned by your Monk features at most once per encounter. Mark it after the first Monk-caused Stunned condition successfully applies. If another of your Monk features would Stun that marked creature later in the same encounter, the creature still makes the required save; on failure it instead loses its Reaction until the end of its next turn. This guard is tracked separately for each Monk.

Temporary maximum-HP reductions caused by Monk features do not stack on the same creature; use the largest reduction from your Monk features. Maximum HP cannot be reduced below 1. Unless a card specifies an earlier end, the reduction lasts until the creature completes a short or long rest. Restoring maximum HP does not restore current HP. These effects are temporary combat trauma, not unstated permanent injuries.

Only one concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; any required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Round recharge ticks once at the start of the Monk's regular initiative turn, including while incapacitated; extra Actions and extra turns never create additional ticks.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. A named ability can receive at most one positive-counter recharge reset or shortening per round. Only an ability whose current recharge counter is above 0 can be reset or shortened.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Monk 1 automatically gains Ki Flow, Unarmored Flow, all three core Stances and basic once-per-round stance switching, then chooses 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Monk 2 chooses 2 additional Base cards. Monk 3 enters Master and chooses 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4 through 8 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice and Martial Apex automatically.

Discipline Initiate is an optional Base selection. Choosing Tank does not grant five free Base abilities: it unlocks the four non-final Tortoise Discipline cards as additional Arch-selection options at their listed Monk levels. Final Form — Bastion of Breath is never a normal selection; at Monk 9 or the first later level when eligible it is gained automatically only if you chose Tank through Discipline Initiate and know at least three of Stone Shell Discipline, Redirecting Palm, Iron Shell Pulse and Echoing Guard. Tortoise Discipline remains compatible with any Hero path chosen later.

At Monk 10 choose Enlightened Master, Iron Fist Master or Way of Shadow and choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch card, including unlocked non-final Tortoise cards. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. At Monk 20 the chosen Hero path's Final is automatic and cannot be selected earlier. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition and scaling gates use Monk class level, not total character level. Normal character proficiency bonus still uses the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock Master, Tortoise Final Form, Hero features or a level-20 Final.

Healing from Monk cards cannot exceed maximum HP, restore the dead or remove Wounds unless explicitly stated. Permanent HP recovery and Ki generation cannot be farmed outside encounters. Resurrection effects are explicitly limited-use. No Monk card can instantly kill a target merely because a descriptive source used language such as Death Touch; death continues to follow the game's ordinary damage and dying rules.

Unarmored Flow completion: while wearing no armor or shield, AC=10+DEX modifier+WIS modifier, or ordinary armorless AC if higher, never both. Unarmed strikes use DEX for attack/damage and 1d6 at 1, 1d8 at 5, 1d10 at 11, 1d12 at 17. This is a new numeric completion; no automatic Extra Attack beyond printed techniques.

Each technique tagged weave creates 1 D in this pilot, unless it explicitly says otherwise. Ki can prevent up to 1 D before resolution only if remaining Ki pays that additional cost. Full-Ki capstones may legally accept D. The Stun Guard shares the suite-wide once/character/target hard-denial mark; its later failed-save fallback of reaction loss is an explicit Monk exception, not a second Stun.

engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Charisma is the Oracle class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Oracle levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Charisma modifier). Revelation attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier. Revelation save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier.

HIT DIE CONFLICT. The class overview registry lists d8, while the detailed Player Rulebook Oracle entry states 6 + Constitution modifier at level 1 and d6 per Oracle level thereafter. This pilot uses the detailed rulebook d6 chassis: 6 + Constitution modifier at Oracle 1 and 1d6 per later Oracle level. The d8 registry value remains a preserved alternative pending owner adjudication.

The Oracle is an exceptional progression class rather than a 25-choice Base/Arch/Hero class. Base Oracle is levels 1-2, Revelation Tier development is the Arch-stage progression at levels 3-9, and Revelation Mastery is the Hero-stage progression at levels 10-20. Mystery and Curse are chosen at level 1 but their later Revelations, Boons and Final abilities remain class-level gated.

Choose exactly ONE Mystery and exactly ONE Curse at Oracle level 1. They are not parallel subclasses that stack. You never gain another Mystery or Curse unless a future explicit retraining or transformation rule says otherwise. Curse limitations are permanent and cannot be removed by ordinary cleansing, curse removal, resurrection or rest.

REVELATION CHARGES are the Oracle's only class power resource. Oracles do not use Resonance Points, spell slots, Weave Dissonance, Overcast or ordinary spell-rank casting for Revelations. Revelation Charges are abbreviated RC. A Revelation card's printed RC cost is paid once before resolution. An illegal activation spends nothing.

RC CAP SCHEDULE for this provisional module: maximum 3 at Oracle levels 1-2, 4 at levels 3-5, 5 at levels 6-8, 6 at levels 9-10 and 7 at level 11+. Increasing the maximum does not automatically refill spent charges except where another feature explicitly says so.

RC RECOVERY. A completed long rest restores RC to maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent RC, never above maximum. Each Mystery has exactly one Prophecy Trigger. During a real encounter, your Prophecy Trigger can restore at most 1 RC per round and never above maximum. Trivial enemies, willing staged targets, summoned sacrifices, repeated corpse abuse, copied damage, copied healing and events generated solely to trigger recovery do not qualify.

A single event can satisfy only one Prophecy Trigger recovery for you even if several descriptions could apply. A Revelation repeated or copied by another feature does not independently trigger Prophecy recovery unless that feature explicitly says it counts as a new Revelation use. Restored charges never recursively trigger another recovery.

At Oracle level 11, the preserved registry draft additionally sets your starting RC when a real encounter begins to at least max(3, your Charisma modifier), capped by your current RC maximum. If you already have more RC, keep the higher current value. This encounter-start floor occurs once per encounter and cannot be triggered by staged initiative.

REVELATIONS are divine class techniques, not ordinary spells. Unless a Revelation explicitly says otherwise, magical silence does not prevent a purely mental Revelation, but a Revelation requiring speech, touch, visible symbolism or another listed component obeys that requirement. Revelations do not generate Dissonance and cannot be modified by spell-slot, RP, spell-rank discount or ordinary spell-proc mechanics.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time unless a specific Oracle feature explicitly creates a narrow exception. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration procedure; if half-damage rounding is required in this pilot, round down. Sustained Revelation control effects grant repeat saves at the cadence printed on the Revelation.

HARD CONTROL GUARD. A creature can suffer at most one Oracle-caused full-turn denial such as Stunned, Paralyzed, Incapacitated by control, or loss of its full Action from your Oracle features per encounter. After that succeeds once, later Oracle effects from you that would fully deny its turn instead remove its Reaction and reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of its next turn after the required save fails.

ADDITIONAL ACTION GUARD. All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. An additional Action cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Features that say a creature acts out of turn use this same cap. Movement-only grants do not count as additional full Actions.

Healing from Oracle features cannot exceed maximum HP, resurrect the dead or remove Wounds unless a feature explicitly says so. Temporary HP never stack. Encounter-only regeneration and drain cannot be farmed outside meaningful combat. Corpse effects create no XP, loot, RC or repeatable corpse resources unless expressly stated.

Copied, echoed, repeated or redirected damage/healing uses only the explicitly copied numeric component. It cannot repeat RC recovery, Prophecy Triggers, action grants, conditions, passive triggers, resource restoration or another copy effect unless the copying feature explicitly says otherwise.

BASE PROGRESSION. At Oracle 1 choose Mystery and Curse; gain the RC engine, Channel Revelation, Prophetic Insight and Divine Sense. At Oracle 2 gain Curse Manifestation, Oracular Trance and Oracle's Burden. No Base feature-selection currency or Skill Points are used.

ARCH-STAGE PROGRESSION. Oracle 3: choose one Tier I Revelation from your Mystery and automatically gain Curse Boon I. Oracle 4: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 5: automatically gain Curse Boon II; any Mystery-specific level-5 feature recorded by the registry belongs to the Mystery module below and does not create an additional generic feature here. Oracle 6: choose one Tier II Revelation and gain Mystery Surge. Oracle 8: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 9: gain your Mystery's fixed Tier III Revelation.

HERO-STAGE PROGRESSION. Oracle 10: gain Curse Boon III and Grand Revelation Foreshadow. Oracle 11: RC cap reaches 7 and the preserved encounter-start RC floor becomes active. Oracle 12: gain the Mystery-specific Mystic Insight. Oracle 13: preserved registry draft grants a second Tier II Revelation; after each completed short rest choose which of your two Tier II Revelations is Attuned for features that specifically refer to an active Tier II option, though both remain known and usable. Oracle 14: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 15: gain Revelation Mastery and Curse Boon IV. Oracle 16: preserved Prophecy Trigger Mastery. Oracle 17: preserved Grand Revelation Foreshadow upgrade. Oracle 18: Prophetic Surge. Oracle 19: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 20: gain the Mystery's Final Revelation and Curse Boon V.

REVELATION MASTERY at level 15 never grants a Revelation you do not know. Choose one mastery enhancement explicitly listed by your Mystery for a Revelation you know. If a listed mastery names a Revelation you did not select, that mastery option is unavailable. Mastery cannot reduce RC below 0, create additional Actions beyond the shared cap or remove repeat-save requirements unless its exact Mystery text says so.

PROPHECY AND DIVINATION never force player beliefs, future choices or confessions. Information features can provide truthful clues, likely outcomes, symbolic visions or current facts, but the Director is not required to reveal unknowable future player decisions. Effects that command or compel a player-controlled character preserve the player's choice of targets and prohibit self-harm, permanent allegiance changes and belief alteration.

CURSE MANIFESTATION provides a common operational intensification rather than ten different hidden sub-engines. When activated, your Curse becomes visibly or metaphysically dominant for 3 rounds: gain +1 on Revelation attacks and +1 to Revelation save DC, but take -1 AC and -1 on your own saving throws for the duration. Any Curse limitation that can normally be voluntarily suppressed cannot be suppressed during Manifestation.

CURSE BOONS are automatic at Oracle levels 3, 5, 10, 15 and 20 for your ONE selected Curse. You do not choose between Curse Boons and do not gain Boons from unselected Curses. Each Curse card below operationalizes all five Boon gates and its permanent limitations.

All class gates use Oracle class level, not total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. Non-Oracle levels do not raise RC maximum, unlock Curse Boons, Revelations, Mystic Insight, Revelation Mastery, Prophetic Surge or Final Revelation.

INTEGRATION PRECEDENCE. The source ceiling draft conflicts with the registry on short rests and extra Revelation activations. This pilot explicitly chooses 1 RC on a completed short rest and permits a second Revelation only through an expressly granted extra Action or double-cast feature, never more than two Revelation resolutions per round. The preserved ceiling alternative is no short-rest recovery and one activation per round; do not combine both configurations.

All combat-triggered RC refunds, including Prophecy, damage riders and Curse Boons, share ONE recovered RC per round. Rest recovery, encounter-start floor and explicitly limited Final refills are separate. A free, copied or refunded use cannot recursively trigger another recovery. Apply this global cap even if an individual card says its recovery is separate.

The shared Prophetic Surge and your Mystery-specific level-18 Prophecy are two descriptions/options of ONE long-rest use, not two charges. Framework cards such as Tier III, Mystic Insight, Mastery and Final Revelation unlock the named Mystery card and never grant duplicate uses. A level-5 registry Mystery label grants no extra unnamed ability.

Oracle zone default: choose at most three allies and three enemies for each pulse or aura benefit, fixed at activation unless the card names fewer. Persistent damaging/healing zones require concentration and at most three pulses. Pay 1 RC before each pulse after the first, or end the effect; once-per-long-rest Finals include their printed pulses in that limited use. One pulse can affect a creature only once per round. Passive personal resistance and a single-target temporary buff are not zones.

Revelation backlash is the local one-turn penalty of -1 to attacks and saves and -5 feet Speed, ending at the end of your next turn. It is not a level of the general Exhaustion condition. Wound Eater's missed-feeding Exhaustion remains the general condition.

Initiative adjustments change order beginning next round. They never produce or erase a regular turn in the current round; a creature still gets at most one regular turn each round. Ties use the original initiative order. Fixed encounter-start bonuses do not retroactively reorder an encounter.

Extra attacks and echoed damage use base weapon/spell dice before critical-hit extra dice. A redirected damage event cannot be reduced a second time, reflected again or generate RC. Charmed alone does not grant command of a creature's actions.

Oracle’s exceptional ASI/feat schedule is 4, 8, 14 and 19. It does not gain extra ASIs at 12 or 16 from the generic class schedule. The rejected five-milestone draft remains in superseded Playtest Overrides for traceability.

engine: Charisma governs Oath DC/M and divine technique attacks. Weapon attacks use their ordinary Strength/Dexterity ability. Hit Die d10; all armor, shields, simple and martial weapons. Paladin has no Conviction or Oracle Revelation Charges. Lay on Hands is its own pool, 5×Paladin level, fully restored only by long rest. Ordinary spells and printed Smite fuel use the same Paladin Core V 2 RP pool; healing points never convert to RP.

Base progression is explicit rather than the ordinary 25-card template: at 1 automatically gain Lay on Hands, Divine Sense, Martial Proficiency, Divine Strike, Protective Stance and Sacred Touch. At 2 gain Righteous Challenge, Bolstering Presence, Fighting Style and ordinary Paladin spell access. At 3 swear ONE of ten Oaths; gain only its Smite modification, Aura and first Revelation spell. This Oath is the Arch specialization. At 10 enter Hero Oath Mastery of that SAME Oath; no second Oath or additional generic Hero tree. Signature Power unlocks 11, Final Gift 20. Oath Revelations automatically unlock 3/5/9/13/17, always known in addition to the shared spell repertoire, rank 1/2/3/4/5 respectively. Exact printed RP costs replace generic cost only if the card explicitly supplies them.

At 2 choose one Fighting Style: Defense +1 AC while armored; Dueling +2 damage to first one-handed melee hit on your own turn; Protection Reaction impose disadvantage on one attack against an adjacent ally when using a shield. At 3 Divine Health gives advantage on disease saves, not universal immunity. At 5 Extra Attack makes two attacks when taking the ordinary Attack Action; named attack techniques use their own counts. These three features reconcile preserved main-registry entries; other old level-table extras, including extra level 14 ASI and undefined free slot riders, are not stacked into this draft. ASI/feat at 4/8/12/16/19 follows general advancement once.

Divine Strike at 1: after one melee weapon hit on your regular turn, spend 1 RP to add S d6 radiant. At 2 this becomes Divine Smite: choose 1 RP for S d6 or 2 RP for(S+1)d8 radiant, once/own turn total. Oath 3 changes type/rider as its card states, never adds another copy of the base damage. Smite is not an ordinary spell, cannot be counterspelled or generically Overcast, and causes no Dissonance. A critical hit doubles Smite damage dice under ordinary rules, but never healing, resources or percentage copies.

One Oath aura, requires consciousness and no concentration. Radius 10 ft at 3, 15 ft at 6, 20 ft at 10, 30 ft at 15. Benefits affect up to 3 allies or 3 enemies as the Oath card states, chosen at start of your turn and changed next turn; they must stay within aura. At 6 choose one additional aura benefit for that day: allies+1 saves against fear/charm, or 1 flat DR against weapon damage. At 7 once/short rest when enemy damages an ally in aura, Reaction make one melee attack if in reach; may pay normal Smite cost even off turn, but total Smite maximum one per round from this reactive feature. At 10 aura persists until start of your next regular turn after incapacitation; then ends if still incapacitated. At 15 also grant selected allies+1 initiative while in aura when initiative is rolled; no retroactive turn changes.

At 17 Aura Surge once/short rest Bonus Action: until start next turn choose up to 3 allies in aura to gain S+M temporary HP and+1 saves. This bounded surge replaces vague doubling of every aura number. At 20 Divine Manifestation makes the aura active upon initiative without an action, radius 30 ft; it ignores ordinary Silence and terrain obstruction between allies but not antimagic explicitly suppressing divine powers, planar barriers or the consciousness rule. Source cannot-be-suppressed language is bounded explicitly. It grants no free Signature, Smite or Revelation spell.

Protected interface: Smite, Aura and Lay on Hands generate no Weave Dissonance. After a successful direct melee hit, your next Oath spell before end next turn generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0, consuming the benefit. No stacking, RP discount or Refrain reset. Oath Revelation spells and the five replacement Forbidden spells below are ordinary spells for strain, countering and concentration; signature powers and final gifts are Oath techniques unless expressly tagged otherwise.

Oath conduct clauses remain intact in source and Oath cards. The Director identifies a relevant clause and a knowingly chosen serious breach before applying a fall. A disagreement, failed roll, coerced act or unknown fact does not silently remove a character. A fall is an explicit story transition recorded with the player: choose the corresponding Oathbreaker inversion or pursue an agreed restoration scene. Preserve class level and already spent resources. Oathbreaker replaces its Oath Aura, Smite rider, Signature and Revelation list, rather than stacking both sets. Base martial abilities remain; Lay on Hands becomes Death Touch using the same current 5 L pool, with no refill on switching.

Death Touch baseline: Action melee divine attack PB+CHA; declare and spend 1 through 2 S+M points before the attack from remaining Lay on Hands pool to deal that much necrotic damage (choose amount before roll; miss still spends declared points). Each Oath inversion may alter type or add its bounded rider; never copy innate traits, confiscate class engines or automatically execute a target. A listed inverted Signature is available only at 11 and replaces the ordinary Signature use, one/short rest. An inverted aura follows the same radius, target cap and timing. Oathbreaker 20 uses the new Black Manifestation common capstone instead of its original Final Gift.

The source names a Forbidden Spell List but does not supply five complete entries for each inversion. This pilot explicitly adds one shared five-spell replacement list (below), with each Oathbreaker using its inversion name as flavor. These are new test rules, not recovered historical spells. Choose the normal Oath package OR inverted package at a time. All later Oath prerequisites still use Paladin class level; the Oathbreaker label does not bypass 3/11/20 gates.

Oath integration limits: one paid Smite total per round, including the level-7 Reaction; one Oath-aura reactive event per round. Multiple damage-redirection options share one event per round unless Crown Undying expressly allows two. Apply original-target defenses once, then split actual damage; transferred damage cannot be mitigated again, reflected, redirected again or generate resources. This explicit rule supersedes wording that permits recipient defenses again.

Sustained Oath spell damage/healing zones use concentration, at most three pulses, and 1 RP upkeep after the first pulse unless a priced card expressly supplies a different finite cadence. Native Oath auras retain their printed passive cadence and target cap. Final auras last their stated finite duration and include their pulses. All hard-denial effects, including compelled Actions, share the common once/source/target/encounter guard; later failures only remove Reactions and reduce Speed by half for one turn.

An emergency Reaction whose trigger itself incapacitates you, such as Grace Reversal or Thorn Crown, may resolve before that incapacitation only if you had a Reaction available before the triggering event. This grants no other actions while incapacitated. Narrative labels such as oppressor require a specific act of captivity/coercion established in the scene, not an alignment or identity assumption.

The source ceiling’s half-pool-per-round Lay on Hands cap is a preserved alternative. This pilot instead uses maximum class level per ordinary Lay on Hands Action and the explicitly once-per-long-rest level-17 Wave that distributes the current remaining pool. No normal heal gains the Wave’s exception.

For any one damage event choose exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Using it consumes the shared redirection allowance for that round. Crown Undying permits two DIFFERENT ally-damage events per round, but still only one redirection feature may modify each event.

cards.name: Beast Empathy
cards.rangeAndTarget: Natural beasts within 30 ft that hear you
cards.effect: Communicate simple emotions/directions. They are not automatically friendly or controlled, cannot answer beyond their experience, and may need normal Animal Handling. No language-based compulsion or extra companion slot.

source.originalText: Beast Empathy: Communicate basic concepts with natural beasts.

engine: Dexterity governs weapons; Wisdom governs primal technique DC/M. This draft uses the detailed book's d8 Hit Die; older runtime d10 remains preserved as a conflicting alternative. At 1 gain Track Target engine: Bonus Action mark one perceived enemy within 90 ft for 1 minute, no RP, one quarry at a time; new mark replaces old. Once/own turn a weapon hit against quarry adds S damage. Mark does not reveal creatures through total cover. Track Target selection is an upgrade, not a second unlock tax.

Weapon Synergy tracks last successful direct weapon hit on your own turns. Changing melee→ranged grants+1 to that ranged attack roll if it is your first attack of the turn; changing ranged→melee makes the hit apply Bleed 1d4 on target's next 2 turns. Once/turn synergy; Do Ts, copies, companions, forced attacks and misses do not advance it. At 5 ordinary Attack Action makes two attacks; techniques use only printed counts. You may draw/stow one weapon as normal object interaction; Dual Style later improves this.

Elemental Attunement is defensive; Elemental Imbue is the separate Pathfinder feature gated 6. Imbue Bonus Action 2 RP, one element for 3 of your turns; once/turn a weapon hit adds 1d4 of chosen element plus fire:Burn 1d4 next target turn, cold:Speed-10 ft until end next turn, poison:CON save or-1 attack rolls until end next turn. Nonstacking; Do Ts never build Hit Chain. Switching element pays again.

Druidic Arrow Combo starts at Ranger 11, not at Base 1. Each direct successful weapon hit adds 1 Hit Chain, maximum 2 gained per regular turn and cap 3. Completing 3 primes one Arrow until end next turn; using it consumes the chain, even on miss. Efficient Killer lowers threshold 2. Chain starts/ends encounters 0, cannot be stocked against allies/captives/summons and is cleared by incapacitation. The Arrow is one Action with a ranged weapon attack or the stated save, costs 0 RP when primed, and is a magical class technique rather than an ordinary spell cast. At most one Arrow per round; it cannot advance its own chain. It requires a wielded bow and ammunition. Ordinary attack/damage riders apply once as printed, never another free arrow.

All Rangers learn five bounded Arrows at 11. Emberroot requires the previous 3 successful weapon hits carried fire imbue: ranged attack, weapon+S d6 fire on hit; up to 2 others within 5 ft take S fire, and primary target Burns 1d4 next turn. Glacial Thorn requires 2 ranged+1 melee among those 3 hits: ranged attack weapon+S d6 cold; on hit STR save or Speed 0 until end next turn. Venomlash requires poisoned/blighted terrain at you or target: ranged attack weapon+S d6 poison; on hit CON save or-1 damage on its next attack. Spirit Fang requires quarry: ranged attack at advantage, weapon+S d6 force; ignores resistance but not immunity on the added force only. Cleansing Grove requires natural terrain at you or target: up to 3 living allies within 10 ft of a point within 60 ft each end Frightened or Poisoned; no attack or damage.

Chosen Hero grants a sixth Arrow at 11. Warder Nature's Wrath: ranged attack weapon+S d6 piercing; up to 2 allies within 10 ft gain M temporary HP (finite mitigation, not repeatable real healing). Stalker Phantom: two ranged attacks against different aligned targets within 60 ft, each weapon damage, no extra dice; one Arrow activation. Outrider Corruption: place 10 ft-radius zone within 60 ft, concentration until start next turn; up to 3 enemies entering/starting there take S d4 necrotic once each, CON half. Arrow copies cannot generate extra attacks, resources or permanent terrain changes.

A successful direct weapon hit between ordinary spell casts clears Refrain and gives the next ordinary spell before end next turn 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0. The benefit is single-use/nonstacking; it reduces neither RP nor both base and repeat separately. Ordinary spells use Ranger rank gates and the shared test magic configuration.

Base choices 1–2, Pathfinder Arch 3–9, and chosen Warder/Stalker/Outrider Hero 10–20 are distinct stages. No source Arch capstone/Finale exists: level 9 receives its normal eligible choice, while 20 automatically improves your Hero Arrow once/long rest (new capstone below). Do not acquire a Hero by spending Base choices. Beast Companion is one permanent bond; it must be a willing/tamed noncorrupted beast with INT<7 and CR no greater than your class level. Its combat profile uses the bounded companion below rather than importing a full CR 20 monster.

If a primed Arrow expires unused, the prime ends and Hit Chain resets to 0. This applies equally to Efficient Killer’s threshold of two. Efficient Killer itself requires Ranger 11, when Hit Chain exists.

cards.name: Balanced Elements
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your own elemental slowing/burning effect
cards.effect: Choose one application: add 1 damage to its next Burn tick OR extend a Speed reduction until end target's following turn. Never extends Stunned, silence, concentration duration or whole-Action denial.

source.originalText: Balanced Elements: Your elemental effects last longer and have secondary effects.

engine: Wisdom is the class ability. Choose Elemental Affinity automatically at 1: Fire, Ice, Air or Earth. Spellcasting/RP remain separate from Totem objects and flasks. Totem capacity 1, rises 2 at 13; any third replaces one of your existing totems. A totem is a visible Tiny magical object: AC 12+PB, HP 2 L, immobile, immune to poison/psychic/conditions, vulnerable to ordinary weapon and other damage. At 0 HP its aura ends. A new totem appears within 30 ft; cannot occupy a creature's space, serve as a bridge, trap a creature without a save or move through walls.

Totem Casting is Action 2 RP, duration 3 of your turns, 15 ft aura. Choose Flame, Stone, Frost, Spirit or Renewal. Benefits require an ally/target in the aura, maximum 3 creatures benefiting per pulse/round chosen by you. Flame adds 1 fire to an ally's first direct weapon hit per round; on critical that target Burns 1d4 next turn. Stone reduces damage by 1 and gives enemies-1 to STR checks to shove. Frost: enemy first entering/starting each round makes CON save or Speed-10 ft until end its turn. Spirit: first necrotic/hex damage per target per round adds 1. Renewal: on start and each of next 2 turns with Bonus Action+1 RP maintenance, up to 3 allies regain 2 HP. Thus Renewal total cost 4 RP for 3 pulses; no free healing on entry. All totems share one concentration burden; losing it ends all. Other concentration effects replace them. Non-Renewal auras need no Bonus Action upkeep. Multiple same-name/stat auras do not stack.

On your turn you may spend Bonus Action to move one totem up to 15 ft along unobstructed ground, remaining within 60 ft. This competes with healing maintenance, companion commands and advanced flasks. Moving an aura over a creature cannot trigger its once/round effect repeatedly. Totem destruction creates no resource return. Once per round, the first ordinary spell cast while inside your own active totem aura generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0; no RP reduction.

The book places Flask Use at Base but describes advanced flask casting as Theurgist/Soothsayer-only. For this draft, Base Flask Use grants mundane prepared tactical flasks thrown with an Action; at Hero 10 only Theurgist/Soothsayer gain magical Bonus Action flasks. Bloodcaller retains mundane alchemical knowledge, not the advanced flask subsystem. At long rest prepare 2 flasks, rising to 3 at 5 and 4 at 11; no encounter refill or stockpiling, total carry cap 4, unused contents become inert when preparing a new batch. This finite-rest supply replaces encounter-based free heal farming.

Flask tier uses S. Mundane Base modes: Burn=one enemy 30 ft DEX save S d6 fire half, failure 1d4 fire next turn; Root=one ground enemy 30 ft STR save Speed 0 until end its next turn; Weaken=one enemy 30 ft CON save or-1 attack damage until end its next turn. Advanced Hero modes additionally: Stun=one enemy 30 ft CON save or no Reactions, failure by 10 Stunned until end its next turn; Heal=one living ally 30 ft S d6+M HP; Restore=end Frightened or Poisoned on one ally 30 ft. Every thrown flask consumes one prepared unit and 2 RP for advanced magic (Base mundane flasks cost 0 RP). Changing payload requires no separate crafting action when throwing. No flask leaves harvestable poison or another flask.

Choose Fire/Ice/Air/Earth bonuses through affinity card; Ember/Cold/Shock damage are fire/cold/lightning, Earth uses bludgeoning. Summoned elemental spirits use one standard companion each, maximum one normally; Elemental Chorus expressly summons a package of 4 but all share one Bonus Action command and a printed combined pulse. Companions cannot generate RP, trigger flask refunds or create corpse/kill farms.

Bloodcaller at Hero 10 transforms permanently into Hagraven, with the player choosing this class path and its stated loss of ordinary Shaman spellcasting. It does NOT lose its RP reservoir: printed Hagraven/Totem techniques still pay RP, but it cannot cast ordinary Shaman spells or advanced magical flasks. It retains prior totem/technique selections. The change is a class choice, not permission for involuntary player-character conversion; ancestry identity and player control remain. At long rest it can prepare mundane flasks only if Base Flask Use is known.

Shaman Base 1–2, Spiritwalker Arch 3–9, and Theurgist/Soothsayer/Bloodcaller Hero 10–20 remain separate stages. Elemental Affinity is automatic 1, not an extra selection cost. No explicit Arch capstone in source:9 has its ordinary choice. At 20 your selected Hero's last active ultimate gains the explicit new capstone improvement below; no new generic Hero class is invented.

cards.name: Improved Concentration
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self
cards.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. This does not alter the DC, protect a Tether from rules that explicitly end both effects, or prevent Silence, incapacitation and other non-damage concentration failures.

source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

cards.name: Knowledge Transfer
cards.rangeAndTarget: One willing ally you touch
cards.effect: Knowledge Transfer. Tags: hero, spellbinder, knowledge. Choose one language you can speak or one skill in which you are proficient. The ally gains proficiency in that language or skill for 1 hour. Expertise is never transferred. The feature conveys functional knowledge, not memories, secrets, class features, spellcasting or tool ownership.

source.originalText: Knowledge Transfer: Temporarily grant an ally knowledge of a skill or language you possess.

cards.name: Arcane Sanctuary
cards.rangeAndTarget: You and up to eight willing creatures within 15 feet
cards.effect: Arcane Sanctuary. Tags: hero, spellbinder, final-theorem, demiplane. Perform a 10-minute ritual to open a temporary demiplane and transport the willing targets inside. For 1 hour creatures inside cannot cast or activate harmful magical effects and magical effects originating outside cannot enter. Nonmagical violence remains physically possible, ordinary healing and communication may function, and creatures can leave through the visible exit as an Action. When the hour ends all occupants return to the entry location or nearest legal spaces.

source.originalText: Arcane Sanctuary: Create a demiplane of safety for 1 hour where harmful magic cannot function (1/week).

engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.
